summary: Atari Games' early polygonal driving-simulation series built around stunt tracks, force-feedback cabinets, manual transmission controls, and later Race Drivin' expansions.

entries.title: Hard Drivin'

emulation.notes: Use arcade hardware or emulation; map steering, shifter, clutch, and pedals carefully.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade simulator output and controls where preserved

primary.why: Hard Drivin' was designed for Atari's arcade simulator cabinet with polygon 3D, a haptic steering wheel, ignition key, four-speed shifter, clutch, and pedals. The many home ports have far less computing power and cannot reproduce the cabinet controls.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version on original hardware or in MAME where supported; Midway Arcade Treasures 2 on GameCube/PS2/Xbox is a compilation access route if owned.

entries.title: Race Drivin'
entries.definitive_edition: Arcade release plus Race Drivin' a Go! Go! extras

emulation.notes: Use arcade route first, then PlayStation emulation for the Go! Go! extras.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade simulator output plus PlayStation-exclusive content

primary.why: Race Drivin' expanded Hard Drivin' with additional tracks, more vehicle choices, linked/buddy race features, and the original arcade force-feedback/manual-control cabinet. The Japan-only PlayStation Race Drivin' a Go! Go! adds extra courses and vehicles, so it is a secondary content route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version through original hardware or supported emulation; then play the Japanese PlayStation Race Drivin' a Go! Go! content for its extra courses and cars.

secondary.exclusive_content: Race Drivin' a Go! Go! adds three courses and increases the vehicle count from three to eight.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Japan-only Race Drivin' a Go! Go! courses and extra vehicles after the arcade primary.
secondary.why: The arcade cabinet is the fidelity route, but this PlayStation version has sourced extra content.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Atari arcade hardware with force-feedback controls; Panorama cabinets used multiple monitors.

entries.title: Hard Drivin' II: Drive Harder

emulation.notes: Use DOSBox for the primary PC route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC DOS output with modern scaling

primary.why: Hard Drivin' II: Drive Harder was a home-system sequel released for Atari ST, Amiga, and MS-DOS rather than as an arcade cabinet. The MS-DOS route has the strongest modern PC preservation and scaling path among sourced platforms.
primary.how_to_play: Play the MS-DOS version in DOSBox with appropriate cycles and input mapping; use Amiga or Atari ST emulation only for platform comparison.

all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced content advantage over the PC route.

all_releases.fidelity: PC home release with modern DOSBox preservation path.
